EDUCATION.DISSTITLE: Multiple Axisymmetric Solutions for Axially Traveling Waves in Solid Rocket Motors

CONGRANT.TITLE: Equipping undergraduates with computational engineering skills for the challenges of tomorrow through project-based learning
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The proposed project seeks to enhance undergraduate STEM education at UTRGV by strengthening computationally intensive courses such as Computational Fluid Dynamics, Blockchain, Machine Learning, Finite Element Analysis, Senior Design, and Undergraduate Research. Through the acquisition of a dedicated computer cluster, the project will provide students with the necessary resources to perform large-scale simulations and data-intensive tasks that are currently impractical, thereby improving the learning experience.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Faculty Seed Research Grant: Laser Surface Texturing based on FEA and CFD Simulations as an Innovative Technique for Addressing Multi-disciplinary Challenges in Engineering Applications
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This study aims to utilize Laser Surface Texturing (LST) in combination with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to improve the performance and longevity of important components in three distinct fields: prosthetic materials, rolling-element bearings, and airfoils. The goal is to enhance the quality of life and industrial performance by increasing the efficiency of prosthetic materials and rolling-element bearings. In airfoils, LST is being explored as a method to reduce drag and improve aerodynamic efficiency. The study involves applying LST to these components and then extensively evaluating the effects through experimentation and computational modeling. The FEA and CFD simulations will provide detailed insights into the performance of the LST-treated surfaces under various operating conditions. The findings of this research project are expected to have significant implications for biomedical engineering, materials science, mechanical engineering, and aeronautics, paving the way for future development and optimization.
